analysis:
The PR changes `darkbloom restart` so the watchdog re-arm always runs after a relaunch attempt, including when it fails.

Code changes:
- RestartCommand.swift head lines 37-40 now wrap stopDrainedProvider plus LaunchAgent.restartAfterDrain in ServiceDrain.relaunchDrainedProvider.
- ServiceDrain+Recovery.swift (patch hunk +38..+53) adds that helper. It runs rearmWatchdog(explicitConfig) via defer on both success and throw.
- Previously, re-arm (base line 49) ran only on success, so a failed start left the provider down with auto-recovery disabled.
- The drain-timeout fence in prepare still throws before the relaunch closure, so a failed drain does not re-arm.

Security relevance:
- This is an availability improvement under T-043 (the watchdog is the same replaceable binary). It adds no new privilege, and the watchdog is not a security authority.
- On the LaunchAgentError.notInstalled path, re-arm now also runs. That could recreate or arm the watchdog plist when the service is not installed. This is an availability/UX consideration, not a security one; the effect depends on rearmWatchdog semantics (source not supplied).
- No change to authorization, attestation (TB-011/T-053), encryption or cache (T-041).

Documentation:
- docs/provider/cli-reference.md head excerpts 861-1720 contain no visible changed-line markers (head text only).
- Content covers env passthrough (DARKBLOOM_APP_ATTEST_WORKER_QUALIFICATION is forwarded only when the value is exactly 1, line 1666), the prefix-cache defaults consistent with T-041, `report` reading auth_token read-only under sudo (line 1452), and logout semantics consistent with A-008.
- No security regression is evident.

For the next pass:
- Verify that rearmWatchdog does not override `[provider] auto_restart=false` or reinstall the watchdog when the provider is not installed.
